experience.title: Senior Data Scientist
experience.description:
Jordan joined Luminary Analytics as its first senior individual-contributor data scientist, hired to build the company’s internal measurement and experimentation capability from scratch.
In her first six months she designed and shipped a self-serve A/B testing framework that reduced the median time from experiment idea to decision from eleven days to under four, a change that the product organisation has described as transformative.
She went on to develop Luminary’s customer health score, a composite metric drawing on product usage, support ticket sentiment, and payment history that the customer success team now uses as their primary churn-risk signal. The model has been credited with a 23% reduction in involuntary churn over the twelve months following its deployment.
In 2023 Jordan led a cross-functional initiative to migrate the company’s analytics warehouse from a legacy MySQL instance to Snowflake, coordinating with engineering, finance, and product stakeholders across a six-month timeline that came in two weeks ahead of schedule and under budget.
She currently manages two junior data scientists and a data analyst, spending roughly a third of her time on mentorship and code review.
Her manager, Sarah Park, has described Jordan as the person most responsible for instilling a culture of measurement at Luminary.

experience.title: Data Analyst
experience.description:
Prior to her time at Luminary, Jordan spent eighteen months as a data analyst within the retail banking division of Cascade Financial, a mid-market financial services firm with roughly 2.4 million retail accounts.
Her primary responsibility was the credit card portfolio analytics function, which she inherited as a collection of roughly forty Excel workbooks maintained by a contractor and transformed into a suite of automated SQL and Python pipelines running on a shared data platform.
Jordan’s most significant contribution at Cascade was a churn prediction model she built to identify retail customers at elevated risk of closing their primary chequing account. The model, which used a gradient-boosted classifier trained on eighteen months of behavioural and transactional data, achieved a precision of 81% at the threshold used in production and was directly integrated into the outbound retention campaign run by the customer experience team.
The campaign achieved a 14-point improvement in 90-day retention for the targeted segment, representing an estimated annualised revenue impact of $3.2 million.
She left Cascade Financial voluntarily in January 2020 to pursue personal commitments and further study, with the full support of her management team.

experience.title: Junior Data Analyst
experience.description:
Jordan’s career began at GrowthMetrics, a boutique analytics consultancy serving early-stage and growth-stage technology startups in the Bay Area.
As one of three junior analysts, she supported client engagements across e-commerce, SaaS, and on-demand logistics, learning to move quickly across different data environments and business contexts.
She contributed to twelve distinct client engagements during her tenure and was solely responsible for delivering three of them during a period of rapid team turnover in early 2018.
Her work at GrowthMetrics gave her an unusually broad foundation: she learned to ask the right business questions before touching a dataset, a habit she has never lost.

education.description:
Jordan graduated from UC Davis with a degree in Statistics, completing a concentration in applied probability and a minor in Computer Science.
Her undergraduate GPA was 3.87.
Her senior thesis, “Predictive Modelling of Urban Transit Ridership Using Bayesian State-Space Models,” was awarded the Department of Statistics Prize for Outstanding Undergraduate Research in 2016.
She was a member of the UC Davis Data Science Club and served as its vice-president in her senior year.

Her statistical toolkit spans classical frequentist inference, Bayesian modelling (Stan, PyMC), survival analysis, and causal inference methods including difference-in-differences and synthetic control.

experience.title: Senior Software Engineer
experience.description:
• Architected a multi-tenant data pipeline in Go and Apache Kafka ingesting 8M events/day
from 200+ enterprise clients; reduced end-to-end latency from 4.2s to 340ms through partition-
key optimisation
• Rebuilt the legacy billing service from Ruby on Rails to a Go microservice; the Ruby codebase
had accumulated 11 years of technical debt and zero test coverage — the rewrite reduced
billing errors by 94% and cut infrastructure costs by $220K/year
• Led a cross-functional project with Java Williams (Staff Engineer, data platform) and Go-
hoon Park (infrastructure lead) to migrate our entire PostgreSQL schema to a multi-tenant
design; Java owned the ETL layer, Ruby (me) owned the API contracts, and Go-hoon owned
the Kubernetes rollout
• Introduced OpenTelemetry-based tracing across 12 backend services written in Go, Python,
and Ruby; built the internal SDK in Go and wrote Ruby bindings so legacy Rails services
could emit traces without a full rewrite
• Contracted Swift Consulting Group to audit our authentication layer; their Rust engineers
identified 3 critical vulnerabilities in our JWT implementation that our Go-based security
scanner had missed
• Mentored 3 engineers, including onboarding our newest hire — a Rails specialist who had
never written Go — through a structured 6-week programme that Ruby (me) designed; all
three are now contributing to production services
• Designed and shipped a self-serve CLI tool in Go (open-sourced as ruby-cli-tools , 1.4K
GitHub stars) that lets customers inspect pipeline health; the name causes occasional con-
fusion in issues when reporters write “Ruby crashed” — they sometimes mean the tool,
sometimes the language

experience.title: Software Engineer II
experience.description:
• Built the core TypeScript and Ruby SDK consumed by 3,000+ customers to instrument
their web applications; Ruby SDK was maintained separately from the Node.js SDK because
legacy customers on Rails could not consume npm packages
• Mentored by Swift Rodriguez (Principal Engineer) on distributed systems patterns; Swift’s
background in iOS development (where Swift the language originated) shaped his architec-
tural instincts — an irony not lost on our team
• Re-implemented the query engine from a Python/Ruby hybrid to a compiled Go binary,
achieving a 12x speedup; the Python layer handled data ingestion, Ruby handled transfor-
mation, and Go handled the aggregation hot path
• Collaborated with Java Williams, then a mid-level engineer at React Analytics, on the
eventing schema; Java later joined me at Python Solutions Inc. and now leads the data
platform there
• Owned the React frontend dashboard (yes, React Analytics Corp. actually uses React, which
creates its own parsing confusion when engineers write “React is slow today” in incident
channels — the company or the library?)
• Built a Datadog integration in Python that exposed 40 custom metrics, and a parallel
Ruby gem that mirrored the same metrics for customers on Rails; maintaining two SDKs in
different languages for the same feature set doubled the maintenance burden
• Participated in on-call rotation for Tier-1 services; wrote 8 post-mortems, 3 of which involved
incidents caused by Ruby’s garbage collector under sustained load on the transformation
service

experience.title: Junior Software Engineer
experience.description:
• Developed RESTful APIs in Node.js and Ruby on Rails for a logistics SaaS platform serving
400+ small business clients; the Node.js services handled real-time event streaming while
the Ruby services handled transactional business logic
• Attended an internal Ruby workshop run by Ruby Frameworks Ltd. (a training company,
unrelated to Ruby the language’s core team); the workshop name was “Ruby for Node.js
Developers” — the audience was Node engineers learning Ruby, which means “Node Tech-
nologies engineers learning Ruby from Ruby Frameworks” in the same sentence
• Wrote Python automation scripts for the data team and contributed Go tooling for the
infrastructure team; by the time I left, I was the only engineer on a 22-person team writing
in Go, Python, Ruby, and Node.js simultaneously
• Resolved 90+ customer bugs across a TypeScript and Ruby monorepo; introduced a triage
labelling convention that differentiated Ruby-language issues from Node-language issues,
reducing misrouted bug reports by 30%

education.degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
education.description:
GPA: 3.74/4.0 Dean’s List: 2014, 2015, 2016
Senior Capstone: Distributed key-value store in Go and C++ implementing the Raft consensus
algorithm.
Relevant coursework: Programming Languages (taught in Python and Ruby), Distributed Sys-
tems (Go), Compilers (using LLVM with a Swift-like toy language), Operating Systems (C,
Rust).
Teaching Assistant: CSCI 349: Ruby and Scripting Languages (2015 – 2016). In this role, Ruby
taught Ruby to first-year undergraduates — the department’s course catalogue literally listed
the TA as “Ruby” and the subject as “Ruby,” which caused scheduling conflicts.

raw.skills:
My primary languages are Ruby (6 years, including Rails, Sinatra, and gem authorship), Go
(5 years, services and CLI tooling), and Python (6 years, data pipelines and scripting). I
write production TypeScript and Node.js and have shipped features in Swift (one iOS ex-
periment during a hackathon), Rust (contributed a Rust rewrite of one hot-path parser at
Python Solutions Inc.), and Java (maintained a legacy Spring Boot service for 14 months at
Node Technologies LLC — the same months during which Java Williams was mentoring me
in system design, so “I was learning Java from Java” is technically accurate). On the data
layer I work most fluently with PostgreSQL and Redis; I have shipped production services
on DynamoDB, Elasticsearch, and ClickHouse. Infrastructure: Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform,
AWS. Observability: OpenTelemetry, Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus. Workflow: Git, GitHub
Actions, Docker, feature flags. I prefer to describe my skill with a language by the production
systems I have shipped rather than a self-assessed proficiency bar, which is why this section is
prose rather than a coloured dot chart.

experience.title: Senior Data Scientist
experience.description:
Jordan joined Luminary Analytics as its first senior individual-contributor data scientist, hired to
build the company’s internal measurement and experimentation capability from scratch. In her first
six months she designed and shipped a self-serve A/B testing framework that reduced the median
time from experiment idea to decision from eleven days to under four, a change that the product
organisation has described as transformative. She went on to develop Luminary’s customer health
score, a composite metric drawing on product usage, support ticket sentiment, and payment history
that the customer success team now uses as their primary churn-risk signal. The model has been
credited with a 23% reduction in involuntary churn over the twelve months following its deployment.

In 2023 Jordan led a cross-functional initiative to migrate the company’s analytics warehouse from
a legacy MySQL instance to Snowflake, coordinating with engineering, finance, and product stake-
holders across a six-month timeline that came in two weeks ahead of schedule and under budget.
She currently manages two junior data scientists and a data analyst, spending roughly a third of
her time on mentorship and code review. Her manager, Sarah Park, has described Jordan as the
person most responsible for instilling a culture of measurement at Luminary.

experience.title: Data Analyst
experience.description:
Prior to her time at Luminary, Jordan spent eighteen months as a data analyst within the retail
banking division of Cascade Financial, a mid-market financial services firm with roughly 2.4 million
retail accounts. Her primary responsibility was the credit card portfolio analytics function, which
she inherited as a collection of roughly forty Excel workbooks maintained by a contractor and
transformed into a suite of automated SQL and Python pipelines running on a shared data platform.
Jordan’s most significant contribution at Cascade was a churn prediction model she built to identify
retail customers at elevated risk of closing their primary chequing account. The model, which
used a gradient-boosted classifier trained on eighteen months of behavioural and transactional data,
achieved a precision of 81% at the threshold used in production and was directly integrated into
the outbound retention campaign run by the customer experience team. The campaign achieved
a 14-point improvement in 90-day retention for the targeted segment, representing an estimated

experience.title: Senior Software Engineer
experience.description:
Architected a multi-tenant data pipeline in Go and Apache Kafka ingesting 8M events/day from 200+ enterprise clients; reduced end-to-end latency from 4.2s to 340ms through partition-key optimisation
Rebuilt the legacy billing service from Ruby on Rails to a Go microservice; the Ruby codebase had accumulated 11 years of technical debt and zero test coverage — the rewrite reduced billing errors by 94% and cut infrastructure costs by $220K/year
Led a cross-functional project with Java Williams (Staff Engineer, data platform) and Go-hoon Park (infrastructure lead) to migrate our entire PostgreSQL schema to a multi-tenant design; Java owned the ETL layer, Ruby (me) owned the API contracts, and Go-hoon owned the Kubernetes rollout
Introduced OpenTelemetry-based tracing across 12 backend services written in Go, Python, and Ruby; built the internal SDK in Go and wrote Ruby bindings so legacy Rails services could emit traces without a full rewrite
Contracted Swift Consulting Group to audit our authentication layer; their Rust engineers identified 3 critical vulnerabilities in our JWT implementation that our Go-based security scanner had missed
Mentored 3 engineers, including onboarding our newest hire — a Rails specialist who had never written Go — through a structured 6-week programme that Ruby (me) designed; all three are now contributing to production services
Designed and shipped a self-serve CLI tool in Go (open-sourced as ruby-cli-tools , 1.4K GitHub stars) that lets customers inspect pipeline health; the name causes occasional confusion in issues when reporters write “Ruby crashed” — they sometimes mean the tool, sometimes the language

experience.title: Software Engineer II
experience.description:
Built the core TypeScript and Ruby SDK consumed by 3,000+ customers to instrument their web applications; Ruby SDK was maintained separately from the Node.js SDK because legacy customers on Rails could not consume npm packages
Mentored by Swift Rodriguez (Principal Engineer) on distributed systems patterns; Swift’s background in iOS development (where Swift the language originated) shaped his architectural instincts — an irony not lost on our team
Re-implemented the query engine from a Python/Ruby hybrid to a compiled Go binary, achieving a 12x speedup; the Python layer handled data ingestion, Ruby handled transformation, and Go handled the aggregation hot path
Collaborated with Java Williams, then a mid-level engineer at React Analytics, on the eventing schema; Java later joined me at Python Solutions Inc. and now leads the data platform there
Owned the React frontend dashboard (yes, React Analytics Corp. actually uses React, which creates its own parsing confusion when engineers write “React is slow today” in incident channels — the company or the library?)
Built a Datadog integration in Python that exposed 40 custom metrics, and a parallel Ruby gem that mirrored the same metrics for customers on Rails; maintaining two SDKs in different languages for the same feature set doubled the maintenance burden
Participated in on-call rotation for Tier-1 services; wrote 8 post-mortems, 3 of which involved incidents caused by Ruby’s garbage collector under sustained load on the transformation service

experience.title: Junior Software Engineer
experience.description:
Developed RESTful APIs in Node.js and Ruby on Rails for a logistics SaaS platform serving 400+ small business clients; the Node.js services handled real-time event streaming while the Ruby services handled transactional business logic
Attended an internal Ruby workshop run by Ruby Frameworks Ltd. (a training company, unrelated to Ruby the language’s core team); the workshop name was “Ruby for Node.js Developers” — the audience was Node engineers learning Ruby, which means “Node Technologies engineers learning Ruby from Ruby Frameworks” in the same sentence
Wrote Python automation scripts for the data team and contributed Go tooling for the infrastructure team; by the time I left, I was the only engineer on a 22-person team writing in Go, Python, Ruby, and Node.js simultaneously
Resolved 90+ customer bugs across a TypeScript and Ruby monorepo; introduced a triage labelling convention that differentiated Ruby-language issues from Node-language issues, reducing misrouted bug reports by 30%
